nodes.subject: Wibree to Bluetooth Low Energy lineage
nodes.object: public Wibree release in October 2006, a June 2007 inclusion agreement, and completed Bluetooth 4.0 integration in early 2010

support_spans.exact_quote: the technology was released to the public in October 2006 with the brand name Wibree.
After negotiations with Bluetooth SIG members, an agreement was reached in June 2007 to include Wibree in a future Bluetooth specification as a Bluetooth ultra low power technology.
The technology was marketed as Bluetooth Smart and integration into version 4.0 of the Core Specification was completed in early 2010.

accepted_phrases: The frozen BLE page traces Wibree's public release in October 2006, a June 2007 agreement to include it in a future Bluetooth specification, and completed integration into Bluetooth 4.0 in early 2010.

nodes.subject: LC3 codec
nodes.object: a royalty-free Bluetooth SIG codec for BLE audio, introduced around Bluetooth 5.2 and succeeding SBC, with comparative claims based on subjective testing and a disputed comparison

support_spans.exact_quote: LC3 ( Low Complexity Communication Codec ) is a royalty-free audio codec specified by the Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) for the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)'s audio protocol and introduced about the time of Bluetooth 5.2 .
It is developed by Fraunhofer IIS and Ericsson , and succeeds the SBC codec .
LC3 provides higher audio quality and better packet loss concealment than SBC and G.722 , with disputed results against Opus , according to subjective testing done by the Bluetooth SIG and ETSI .

accepted_phrases: The frozen LC3 page identifies LC3 as a Bluetooth SIG BLE-audio codec introduced around Bluetooth 5.2 and succeeding SBC; its comparative quality passage is explicitly tied to subjective tests and includes a disputed comparison, so it is not a universal endpoint guarantee.

nodes.subject: audio coding and codec implementation
nodes.object: a format does not dictate every codec algorithm, lossy coding irretrievably removes information, and streamed audio is commonly lossy-compressed for distribution

support_spans.exact_quote: An audio coding format does not dictate all algorithms used by a codec implementing the format.
A lossy audio coding format additionally reduces the bit resolution of the sound on top of compression, which results in far less data at the cost of irretrievably lost information.
Transmitted (streamed) audio is most often compressed using lossy audio codecs as the smaller size is far more convenient for distribution.

accepted_phrases: The coding-format page separates format from codec implementation, says lossy coding irretrievably removes information, and says streamed audio is commonly lossy-compressed for convenient distribution.

High output impedance can result in frequency response fluctuations, due to varying load impedance at different frequencies.
The introduction of digital signal processing (DSP) technology led a number of manufacturers to introduce amplifiers with 'headphone virtualization' features.
